precepts.text: Then certain ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king. You will always have certain ungodly men and women among us who hate their own people. Videos played in class of black commentators on the Carmelo Anthony verdict: one celebrated the guilty verdict and blamed the family for spending the defense fund; another said he was overjoyed there were no black people on the jury. Whatever happened to a jury of your peers? That is the same thing they did back then: an all-white jury, and a judge that allowed it, with connections to the other family. A video was also played of a woman calling black supremacy the most dangerous ideology and saying every race is tired of black people; the teaching point: where does black supremacy exist? She is not the only one who thinks like that, and there are even those calling themselves repented Israelites who think exactly like that. We had a bunch of them leave in 2018.
precepts.point: For he saw that it was impossible that the state should continue quiet, and Simon leave his folly, unless the king did look thereunto. Blessed are the peacemakers, but peace does not always work with some people; some spirits are grimy, and at the end of the day they don't want peace with you.
precepts.why:
Simon hated Onias so much that one of his faction murdered one of Onias’s priests, and he got Apollonius, the governor of Coelosyria and Phenice, to rage and “increase Simon’s malice.” Not only did he turn his own group against the high priest; he went to the other nations against him. That is how far your anger goes when you cannot get your way.

That spirit shows up again in 1 Maccabees: “Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower.” You will always have that: certain ungodly men and women among us who hate their own people and run to the king.

See how it relates to us today. On the Carmelo Anthony verdict, one black commentator celebrated the guilty verdict and blamed the family for spending the money raised for his defense on houses. Another said he was overjoyed there were no black people on the jury. Whatever happened to a jury of your peers? It is the same thing they did back then: a whole white jury, and a judge who allowed it, with connections to the other family. Whatever the white man did, not guilty; a black man on trial, three or four minutes, guilty.

Then a black woman called black supremacy the most dangerous ideology in the world and said every race is tired of black people, and “we” want y’all gone. Where does black supremacy exist? Nobody has ever seen it. And she is not the only one who thinks like that. There are brothers and sisters calling themselves repented Israelites who think exactly like that; we had a bunch of them leave in 2018.

Onias went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all.” The ungodly who hate their own people go to the king to accuse them. That is the difference between Onias and Simon.

precepts.why:
“Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. You have to hate your own people to betray them. That is the young man in the red MAGA hat who said he would deport his own parents for not having Esau's paperwork. That paperwork means nothing; the earth belongs to us, and our paperwork is the Bible.

How can one of our own do that? Paul answers: “Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel”. The word of God is not going to fail; it has not failed. But they are not all Israel which are of Israel.

Just because somebody looks like you, speaks the same language as you and eats the same foods as you does not mean they are of your people. We have to be aware of this.

Esau in his witchcraft tells our young men, join the military, you will explore and experience the world, your family will be good, we will give you college tuition. What he does not tell you is that you have to go to the countries of your people and oppress them and kill them. Poor whites and mainly poor blacks and Latinos go out in Esau's military and kill people who look just like them: in Panama, Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua, Libya, Iraq. They are going to rat us out; our own people who hate us will betray us, as they did Jonathan.

precepts.why:
Christ said it would come to this: “And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.” Because sin shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold: emotionless, no empathy, no feelings for your people, not even for your parents. That is what we are seeing in the ungodly persons who hate their own people and go to the king to betray them.

If they are doing that now, imagine when we are making noise. They are already passing laws and putting a media blackout on us. It is going to get to such a level that they will want to put us to death, thinking they are doing good and saving the people.

But it is only betrayal, and their salvation in Esau's kingdom is only for a moment. There is a judgment for betraying your people. Look at Judas, the main betrayer: he betrayed Christ for thirty pieces of silver, and he killed himself, because he knew what he did was evil. The red MAGA hat gives you no superpowers. It does not hide your brown skin or your black skin; it just makes you look more and more like a clown, like a traitor.

precepts.point: There is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land. Evil was among Israel before the white man; it only multiplied under him.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
When the Greeks came into power, the evils of our people multiplied, the same evils that were already among us in Moses' time. First Maccabees shows it: “Then came ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower”. Our own people, who hated their people, ran to Massa to tell on our brother Jonathan, who loved his people. Rats.

And Hosea 4:1 is before the Europeans came into power at all. “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land”: he is talking to Israelites in our own land, and his issue is with us. “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” No truth, no laws, no mercy or kindness among our people. We were being evil: “By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood.” Brother kills brother, brother kills sister, sister kills sister.

“Therefore shall the land mourn”: God said, I am going to take away all your resources, and have the heathen come in, destroy you and take your possessions, because of all the evil you are doing among yourselves.

Black folks love to point the finger and say the white man made us evil. No. Evil was always among us; it just multiplied when we got around this man. All skinfolk ain't kinfolk: those ungodly persons who hated their own people and ran to the king were our own, and they still are.

points: Then certain ungodly persons who hated their own people. Certain ungodly persons, like this president. This man hates his own people. He would rather have power. He would rather have wealth. He would rather be on the side of evil. He would rather see his people destroyed for his own personal gain.

Went unto the king, and told him that Jonathan besieged the tower. He went unto Donald Trump. And ratted on his people, turned on his people, betrayed his people. It is the same thing over and over again. We are always going to have traitors amongst our people.

Then certain ungodly persons, who hated their own people, went unto the king. The Chinese lady made a point to say black jurors found the man who shot the boy not guilty. There has always been a certain remnant of our people who love other races better than their own. What was true during the time of the Maccabees is true today: you have got Christians who hate their own people.

And on the handout talking point: everybody knows the Asian community had a hand out. When the government was giving them loans to open businesses in the black community, the government was denying black people loans; that is documented history. And during World War II, when America put the Japanese in internment camps, they paid them reparations when they let them out. So it is very amusing that they use this talking point on us.
